budgeting_multiple_currencies.tips_choose_the_currency_you_think_in: Choose the currency you think in. Usually where you pay rent. All your budgeting targets should be in this currency.
budgeting_multiple_currencies.tips_manual_fx_conversion_is_the_fastest: Manual FX conversion is the fastest way to burn out on budgeting. Use a tool that does it for you.
budgeting_multiple_currencies.tips_add_a_3_5_buffer_to: Add a 3-5% buffer to categories affected by currency swings. This prevents your budget from breaking when rates move.
budgeting_multiple_currencies.tips_your_spending_reports_should_roll_u: Your spending reports should roll up to one display currency so you can see the real picture. Looking at separate currency totals is misleading.
budgeting_multiple_currencies.tips_moving_money_between_currencies_is_: Moving money between currencies is not spending. Make sure your tool does not count FX transfers as expenses.

best_ynab_alternatives.faqs_it_depends_on_what_made_you: It depends on what made you leave. If you want YNAB's zero-based method with multi-currency, privacy, and a lower price, Budgero is the closest match. If you're in the US and want automatic bank sync with investment tracking, Monarch Money. If you want completely free and don't mind self-hosting, Actual Budget. If you think in forecasts rather than envelopes, PocketSmith.
best_ynab_alternatives.faqs_is_there_a_free_ynab_alternative: Is there a free YNAB alternative?
best_ynab_alternatives.faqs_yes_several_actual_budget_is_free: Yes, several. Actual Budget is free and open source (self-hosted). EveryDollar has a genuinely usable free tier with manual entry. Goodbudget offers a limited free tier. Budgero Self-Host is free forever on your own server with the full feature set — and Budgero Cloud has a 35-day free trial with no card required.

best_ynab_alternatives.faqs_most_us_budgeting_apps_monarch_simp: Most US budgeting apps (Monarch, Simplifi, EveryDollar) simply don't work in Europe. The realistic European options are Budgero (multi-currency, EU data hosting, EUR/GBP billing), PocketSmith (international bank feeds), and Actual Budget (self-hosted). See our dedicated YNAB alternative for Europe guide for the full breakdown.
best_ynab_alternatives.faqs_what_is_the_best_self_hosted: What is the best self-hosted YNAB alternative?
best_ynab_alternatives.faqs_two_serious_options_actual_budget_f: Two serious options: Actual Budget (free, open source, single-currency) and Budgero Self-Host (free, 168 currencies, encryption built in). Both run in Docker on a NAS, Raspberry Pi, or VPS. Our self-hosted YNAB alternative guide walks through setup for both.
best_ynab_alternatives.faqs_which_ynab_alternatives_support_mul: Which YNAB alternatives support multiple currencies?
best_ynab_alternatives.faqs_only_three_apps_in_this_comparison: Only three apps in this comparison handle multi-currency properly: Budgero (168 currencies in one budget with live FX rates), PocketSmith (multi-currency accounts with daily rate updates), and Lunch Money (multi-currency tracking). YNAB itself, Monarch, Simplifi, EveryDollar, Goodbudget, and PocketGuard are all effectively single-currency.
best_ynab_alternatives.faqs_three_reasons_come_up_constantly_pr: Three reasons come up constantly: price ($109/yr and rising), US-centricity (bank sync barely works outside North America and there's no multi-currency support), and data privacy (budgets are stored on YNAB's servers in readable form). Which of those bothers you most should drive which alternative you pick.

self_hostable.faqs_anything_that_runs_docker_a_raspber: Anything that runs Docker. A Raspberry Pi 4 (4GB+) is enough for a single user. A NAS, a small home server, or a $5/month VPS will comfortably handle a household. Budgero is a small Go binary and a SQLite-backed database — there is no Postgres, no Redis, no message queue, no Java. Resource use stays under 200MB of RAM in normal operation.
self_hostable.faqs_can_i_run_budgero_on_a: Can I run Budgero on a Synology, Unraid, or QNAP NAS?
self_hostable.faqs_yes_synology_dsm_unraid_qnap_contai: Yes. Synology DSM, Unraid, QNAP Container Station, and TrueNAS all run the official Budgero Docker image without modification. You point a single port at the container, mount a persistent volume for the SQLite database, and you are done. The full setup guide covers the NAS-specific paths.
self_hostable.faqs_does_self_hosted_budgero_work_on: Does self-hosted Budgero work on a Raspberry Pi?
self_hostable.faqs_yes_budgero_ships_multi_arch_docker: Yes — Budgero ships multi-arch Docker images (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64), so a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 works out of the box. A Pi Zero 2 W will technically run it, but for responsiveness a Pi 4 is recommended.
self_hostable.faqs_yes_for_any_deployment_beyond_local: Yes — for any deployment beyond localhost, Budgero needs to be served over HTTPS. The zero-knowledge encryption runs in the browser via the Web Crypto API (window.crypto.subtle), which browsers only expose in secure contexts (HTTPS, or http://localhost). For LAN-wide or remote access the easiest path is a reverse proxy with automatic Let's Encrypt — Caddy is the simplest, Traefik and Nginx Proxy Manager also work well. If you'd rather skip certs entirely, Tailscale (HTTPS MagicDNS) and Cloudflare Tunnel both terminate TLS for you and require no port forwarding.
self_hostable.faqs_how_do_i_back_up_my: How do I back up my self-hosted Budgero data?
self_hostable.faqs_all_data_lives_in_a_single: All data lives in a single SQLite file inside the volume you mounted. Snapshot the volume, copy the file with `docker cp`, or use any standard SQLite backup tool. Because Budgero is end-to-end encrypted on the device, even if you store backups in third-party cloud storage, the contents stay encrypted under your master password.
self_hostable.faqs_how_do_updates_work_for_self: How do updates work for self-hosted Budgero?
self_hostable.faqs_pull_the_latest_docker_image_and: Pull the latest Docker image and restart the container. Database migrations run automatically on startup. The app shows a dismissable notice when a newer release is available, but you decide when to upgrade — the running container will keep working on the version you deployed for as long as you want. The Self-Hostable changelog is published alongside Cloud releases.
self_hostable.faqs_can_i_run_budgero_air_gapped: Can I run Budgero air-gapped (fully offline)?
self_hostable.faqs_yes_there_is_no_telemetry_no: Yes. There is no telemetry, no license check, no analytics. The only routine outbound call is an update check against budgero.app, at most every 12 hours, that carries your install's version and build number and nothing else — set UPDATE_CHECK_DISABLED=true and it never fires, with no loss of functionality. Optional currency exchange rates (a free public dataset on the jsDelivr CDN, no API key) are the only other outbound call — and CURRENCY_API_BASE_URL can point them at your own mirror. You can run Budgero on a fully isolated network indefinitely.
self_hostable.faqs_how_do_i_import_my_ynab: How do I import my YNAB data into self-hosted Budgero?
self_hostable.faqs_export_your_ynab_budget_as_csv: Export your YNAB budget as CSV and use the import flow inside Budgero. Categories, transactions, and account structure come across. The import preview lets you confirm before anything is written, so you can iterate until the mapping is right.
self_hostable.faqs_what_about_authentication_and_multi: What about authentication and multi-user access?
self_hostable.faqs_self_hosted_budgero_handles_authent: Self-hosted Budgero handles authentication locally. You create accounts directly on your instance, and each user has their own encrypted workspace. For households, you can run a shared instance and invite household members. There is no SSO out of the box, but the auth layer is designed so you can put it behind your own reverse proxy (Authelia, Authentik, Tailscale) if you want.
self_hostable.faqs_yes_budgero_is_open_source_under: Yes. Budgero is open source under the AGPL-3.0, an OSI-approved license — the same license used by Firefly III. The full source code is published on GitHub: you can read, audit, modify, self-host, redistribute — and contribute to — it; the AGPL's one condition is that if you offer a modified version over a network, you must share your modified source with its users. We are a small commercial project funded by the Cloud edition; self-hosters get a free Docker image with the full feature set, no license keys, no feature gating, and no telemetry beyond a disable-able daily update check (a version number, nothing else). Because the code is open source, your ability to keep running Budgero doesn't depend on our continued operation.

self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_yes_budgero_is_open_source_under: Yes — Budgero is open source under the AGPL-3.0, an OSI-approved license. The full source code is public on GitHub: you can read, audit, modify, self-host, redistribute — and contribute to — it; the AGPL's condition is that offering a modified version over a network requires sharing your modified source with its users. Self-hosters get a free Docker image with the full feature set, no license keys, and no feature gating, running on your own infrastructure under your control. Because the code is open source, what you run today keeps working regardless of what happens to the company.
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_pull_the_docker_image_copy_the: Pull the Docker image, copy the example docker-compose.yml, set a few environment variables (database URL, JWT secret, base URL), and docker compose up. Typical setup is under 10 minutes on a fresh VPS. There is a full walkthrough in the self-host documentation.
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_what_hardware_do_i_need_to: What hardware do I need to self-host?
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_very_little_budgero_runs_comfortabl: Very little. Budgero runs comfortably on any VPS with 1 vCPU and 1 GB of RAM. A €4–€6/month DigitalOcean, Hetzner, or OVH droplet is more than enough for a household. Raspberry Pi 4 also works.
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_is_the_self_hosted_version_as: Is the self-hosted version as fully-featured as Cloud?
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_yes_self_host_is_the_same: Yes. Self-host is the same codebase as Cloud. You get zero-based budgeting, 168-currency multi-currency support, end-to-end encryption, offline PWA, YNAB import, shared budgets, AI-powered categorization (bring your own LLM or local Ollama), the push API, and everything else. The only difference is we do not manage the hosting, updates, or backups for you.
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_what_if_i_want_to_stop: What if I want to stop self-hosting later?
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_export_your_data_from_self_hosted: Export your data from self-hosted Budgero, then import it directly into Budgero Cloud. There is no lock-in in either direction. Your encrypted SQLite database is yours, in a standard format.
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_self_host_backups_are_your_responsi: Self-host backups are your responsibility. Budgero's database is a single SQLite file (encrypted end-to-end with your key), so backup is as simple as scheduling a nightly copy to S3, Backblaze B2, or another server. The documentation includes a sample backup script. Because data is encrypted client-side, your backup storage provider cannot see your financial data even if they wanted to.
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_can_i_use_a_custom_domain: Can I use a custom domain?
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_yes_point_your_domain_at_your: Yes. Point your domain at your server, put a reverse proxy (Caddy, Traefik, nginx) in front of Budgero, and you get a TLS-terminated, custom-domain deployment. The documentation has reference configs for Caddy and Traefik.
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_will_there_be_updates_and_new: Will there be updates and new features?
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_yes_we_ship_new_features_continuous: Yes. We ship new features continuously to the main branch, and tag stable Docker images. Self-hosters pull the latest image on their own schedule. You will never be forced to update, but you also will not miss out on improvements if you want them.
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_can_i_import_my_ynab_budget: Can I import my YNAB budget into self-hosted Budgero?
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_yes_budgero_ingests_ynab_export_fil: Yes. Budgero ingests YNAB export files directly — categories, transactions, budget groups, accounts, history. Same import flow as Cloud. Takes about 5 minutes.
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_how_does_self_hosted_budgero_compar: How does self-hosted Budgero compare to Actual Budget?
self_hosted_ynab_alternative.faqs_actual_budget_is_the_other_major: Actual Budget is the other major self-hosted, open-source YNAB-style app. We like Actual and think it is a great project. The differences most people care about: Budgero supports 168 currencies natively in a single budget with live FX rates (Actual is largely single-currency). Budgero includes end-to-end encryption with zero-knowledge server architecture. Budgero ships a fully managed Cloud option if you ever stop wanting to run servers yourself. If you only need single-currency budgeting on your own box, Actual is a fine choice. If you need multi-currency or want a Cloud fallback, Budgero is the better fit.

privacy.budgero_sets_no_analytics_or_advertising: Budgero sets no analytics or advertising cookies and runs no advertising trackers, so there is no cookie banner. Product analytics in Budgero Cloud are cookieless and pseudonymous, never include your financial data, and can be switched off in Settings → Security & Privacy. Self-hosted Budgero sends no telemetry at all. See §3.5 and §8.

This is on by default, on the basis of legitimate interest (§4), and you can switch it off at any time (see below). Self-hosted Budgero sends no analytics or telemetry of any kind.

Before login, a random identifier is used that exists only in memory for that visit. Your name and email address are not sent to the analytics provider.
privacy.some_events_are_sent_by_the_server: Some events are sent by the Budgero server instead of your browser — for example sign-up, subscription changes, workspace and invitation changes, push-sync tokens, and the outcome of requests the server handles for bank sync or the AI assistant. privacy.cookieless_the_analytics_library_keeps: Cookieless: the analytics library keeps its identifiers in memory only and writes nothing to cookies, localStorage or sessionStorage on your device.
privacy.names_of_transactions_accounts_categorie: names of transactions, accounts, categories or payees, amounts, balances, dates, notes, the text of AI conversations or anything else you type into your budget, error message text, session recordings, automatic click capture (autocapture), heatmaps or surveys.
privacy.settings_security_privacy_in_the_app: Settings → Security & Privacy in the app. The choice is saved to your account, applies on all your devices, and also stops the server-side events. Budgero works exactly the same with analytics switched off.
privacy.on_the_budgero_website_page_views: On the Budgero website, page views and clicks on buttons such as “Start free trial” are counted to understand how people find the product. Two tools are used, and neither stores anything on your device:
privacy.umami_desc: — self-hosted by Budgero, so no third party receives the data, and never linked to your Budgero account. It sets no cookies and stores nothing on your device. Your IP address is used only at the moment of the request to look up an approximate location (country, region and city) and is not stored. Visits are grouped by a keyed hash of your IP address and browser that changes at the start of every calendar month, so Umami can’t recognise you from one month to the next. It records the page, referrer, browser, operating system, device type, screen size and language, and Budgero uses it only as aggregate visit statistics. Umami also counts the steps of the sign-up flow in the app.
privacy.posthog_website_desc: — cookieless on the website too, so nothing is stored on your device. PostHog derives a visitor identifier on its own servers from a hash of your IP address, browser and the website’s hostname, combined with a salt that changes every day and is then deleted. Visits on the same day can be counted together, but you can’t be recognised from one day to the next, and website visits are never linked to your Budgero account. Your IP address isn’t used for location and isn’t stored with these events. PostHog is not loaded on the website when your browser sends a Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track signal.

privacy.legitimate_interest_in_improving_and_fix: Legitimate interest in improving the product and fixing errors — Art. 6(1)(f). privacy.budgero_uses_no_analytics_advertising_or: Budgero uses no analytics, advertising or other non-essential cookies, and no third-party advertising scripts. privacy.strictly_necessary_storage_desc: — your login session (set by the authentication provider, Clerk), your encrypted budget data kept on your device for offline use and sync, and preferences such as language. Always on; it can’t be disabled, because the service doesn’t work without it.

zero_based_budgeting.zero_based_budgeting_is_a_method: Zero-based budgeting is a method where every dollar of income is assigned to a specific category before you spend it. At the end of the month, your income minus your budgeted amounts equals zero. Not because you spent everything, but because every dollar has a purpose.
zero_based_budgeting.zero_based_budgeting_forces_intentional_: Zero-based budgeting forces intentional decisions. Instead of wondering where your money went, you decide where it goes before you spend it.
zero_based_budgeting.the_method_works_because_it_eliminates: The method works because it eliminates the gap between intention and action. When you assign $400 to groceries, you are not hoping you will spend less than $400. You are committing to it.
zero_based_budgeting.it_also_surfaces_trade_offs_when: It also surfaces trade-offs. When every dollar is assigned, adding $50 to dining out means taking $50 from somewhere else. That friction is the point. It makes spending decisions conscious rather than automatic.
zero_based_budgeting.people_who_use_zero_based_budgeting: People who use zero-based budgeting consistently report feeling more in control of their finances, even when their income has not changed. The awareness alone changes behavior.
zero_based_budgeting.zero_based_budgeting_requires_the_most: Zero-based budgeting requires the most effort but gives you the most control. If you are reading this page, you probably want that control.
zero_based_budgeting.start_with_last_month_s_bank: Start with last month's bank statement to estimate expenses. You do not need to guess. Use real numbers.
zero_based_budgeting.do_not_try_to_be_perfect: Do not try to be perfect the first month. Your categories will evolve as you learn where your money actually goes.
zero_based_budgeting.budget_for_irregular_expenses_car_mainte: Budget for irregular expenses (car maintenance, annual subscriptions, gifts) by spreading them across months. This prevents surprise budget busters.
zero_based_budgeting.review_your_budget_weekly_for_the: Review your budget weekly for the first few months, then monthly once you find your rhythm.

updates.u_f2822d28bf93: Full disclosure: Budgero is our product, so judge this entry accordingly. It exists because YNAB's method works but its US-centricity doesn't — Budgero keeps zero-based budgeting and adds the things international users keep asking for: real multi-currency, end-to-end encryption, offline mode, optional zero-knowledge bank sync (bring your own SimpleFIN or Enable Banking connection), and a free self-host edition. If you want bank sync with zero setup, or investment tracking, pick Monarch or PocketSmith instead.
